curated-fs-styro-gf-victor-mono: Victor Mono sets its monospace letters loosely, with bowls left open on one side and a size that looks magnified. Bump its size up a notch against Styro's crowded retro heading.
curated-fs-styro-montserrat: Styro brings a retro, crowded swagger, with letters jammed nearly shut (handy for an art deco invitation, say). And Montserrat glides along below it, round and geometric, with plenty of white space leading into each curve.
curated-fs-tanker-fs-paquito: Tanker's heavy letters turn every open curve inward, packed tight, with lowercase that looks huge beside its capitals. Paquito, a classic serif, stays confident underneath; give it a bit more size.
curated-fs-telma-archivo: Soft, pen-written grace comes first, as Telma's thin strokes run about half the weight of its thick ones. Archivo, a plain sans with a commanding x-height, would carry a longer passage briskly.
curated-fs-telma-gf-anek-latin: Anek Latin stands tall, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals while its curves stay held open. Under Telma's flowing script, a longer passage would read cleanly, though the pair is happiest with a few lines.
curated-fs-telma-gf-anek-telugu: Loose pen strokes, gentle and unhurried. Telma carries a faint swell in each curve like pulled taffy, while Anek Telugu's wide, tall bowls would set a steady, open rhythm across a longer passage.
curated-fs-telma-gf-arimo: Understated, that's Telma's first impression, with a high mean line and a wide-mouthed a. Arimo, a plain sans with spacious gaps in its rounded glyphs, takes over once the text starts to run on.
curated-fs-telma-gf-armata: Graceful script leads here, maybe on a seed packet, with Telma's wide-mouthed a and high mean line. Make the heading too small and its sturdy thin lines would fade, while Armata, a sans-serif, copes fine with a bit more size.
curated-fs-telma-gf-arsenal: Arsenal keeps its sans-serif letters close-knit, with a x-height nearly matching the caps. Next to Telma's flowing pen script, it feels grounded and brisk, a quiet foil to all that graceful movement.
curated-fs-telma-gf-atkinson-hyperlegibl: Telma writes with a wide-mouthed a and a high mean line, its hairlines sturdy enough to hold up. Atkinson Hyperlegible, a sans-serif with wide-set terminals on s, would make a longer passage feel plain and approachable.
